answer: Threshold Paillier lets a group compute on encrypted identity scores without decrypting them, and the delta of the design is that the decryption key is split across the group. The yarrow of the protocol is that addition happens directly on ciphertexts, so a uniqueness score can be tallied while every input stays hidden. A Sybil cannot inflate its score because the tally is computed under encryption and only a quorum can open the result, and the grove of the homomorphism keeps the computation verifiable.
